steps.title: Import input/output and array support
steps.note: iostream reads the board size and prints the result. vector stores the two-dimensional board.

steps.title: Store the board and its size
steps.note: n is the board width and height. A value of -1 means a square has not been visited.

steps.title: Define the eight knight moves
steps.note: Each move changes one coordinate by two squares and the other by one. Matching indices of dr and dc form one legal offset.

steps.title: Declare the recursive search
steps.note: row and col describe the current square; visitedCount counts squares already included in the route.

steps.title: Recognize a complete tour
steps.note: There are n*n board squares. Reaching that many visits is success. No closing-edge condition is imposed.

steps.title: Try each destination
steps.note: Loop through the eight offsets and compute the destination from the current square.

steps.title: Reject invalid candidates
steps.note: Skip out-of-bounds coordinates before indexing the board, then skip squares that have already been visited.

steps.title: Choose the candidate
steps.note: Write the visit number into the destination so later recursive calls cannot reuse it.

steps.title: Continue recursively
steps.note: Search from the new square with one more visited square. Propagate success immediately.

steps.title: Undo an unsuccessful choice
steps.note: Reset the square to -1 so another branch can use it. This is the essential backtracking operation.

steps.title: Report failure of this branch
steps.note: After all eight choices fail, return false to the previous search call.

steps.title: Read and validate the demonstration input
steps.note: Accept board sizes 1 through 5. The upper limit is a demonstration restriction because exhaustive search can be expensive.

steps.title: Initialize the start
steps.note: Fill every square with -1, then number the starting square (0,0) as visit 0.

steps.title: Run the search and handle failure
steps.note: One square is already visited, so call knightTour(0,0,1). A false result means the exhaustive search found no route for this board and start.

steps.title: Print the completed board
steps.note: Each value identifies the order in which its square was visited. There are n*n different values, from 0 to n*n-1.
